::: {.lead}
Introductions, how the study will work, and what the Kitáb-i-Íqán is — no reading is assigned
for this first session.
:::

## Introductions

- Your name, and where you're from
- What you want to study in college, or what career you have in mind (if you know yet)
- Your experience of reading the Writings, on your own or in groups
- What you hope to get out of this year, and out of this study
- Something fun you did this summer

## Goals of the study

1. To develop the habit of reading the Writings by yourself
2. To advance in your understanding of fundamental Bahá'í beliefs, and how to explain them to others
3. To experience the joy of reading the Sacred Writings

## How the sessions work

- Most of our time goes on discussing and reflecting on the text itself.
- Part of each session takes up the paragraphs assigned for that week; part is spent reading and
  reflecting together on selected paragraphs, which will be printed and brought to the session.
- We can supplement the study with other activities, games or art, based on your ideas — say what
  you'd like.
- Further resources are posted for anyone who wants to follow a topic further. They are never
  required reading.
- There is a break in the middle of every session.

## What we expect of each other

- To contribute to an open and welcoming environment, and to respect everyone in the group.
- To come having read the paragraphs, having made an honest attempt to engage with the text and
  reflect on its meaning.
- To ask the questions you actually have, and to respond to what others say.
- To be open to changing your mind when someone else's idea is better than yours — and to make
  your best effort to say what you think when you disagree.
- To use phones only for the study: looking up a definition, or getting to the text.
- **You are not expected to understand everything we read.** That is why we study together.

## What is the Íqán?

The Kitáb-i-Íqán — the Book of Certitude — was revealed by Bahá'u'lláh in Baghdád in 1862, in
answer to questions from one of the maternal uncles of the Báb. It was translated by Shoghi
Effendi and first published in English in 1931.

For the setting in which it was revealed — the state of the Bábí community, the two years in
Kurdistán, and the years in that house in Baghdád — see [Context](../context.qmd). Shoghi
Effendi's own account of the Book is on the [Summary](../summary.qmd) page.

## The three maternal uncles of the Báb

The Báb had three maternal uncles, brothers of His mother, Fáṭimih-Bagum.

1. **Ḥájí Mírzá Siyyid Muḥammad** — *Khál-i-Akbar*, the Greater Uncle. The eldest of the three,
   and the recipient of the Íqán.
2. **Ḥájí Mírzá Siyyid ʻAlí** — *Khál-i-Aʻẓam*, the Greatest Uncle. The middle brother, who took
   charge of the Báb's upbringing after His father died. Having seen His qualities from
   childhood, he recognized the station of the Báb at once and became an ardent believer soon
   after the Declaration — the first to declare his faith after the Letters of the Living, and
   both a promoter of the new Faith and a protector of its Founder. Refusing to recant, he was
   publicly martyred as one of the Seven Martyrs of Ṭihrán, a few months before his Nephew.
3. **Ḥájí Mírzá Siyyid Ḥasan-ʻAlí** — *Khál-i-Aṣghar*, the Lesser Uncle. The youngest of the
   three.

## How the questions came to be asked

Before His Declaration, the Báb was in Bushihr, in business with His three uncles. He left for
Shíráz accompanied by Khál-i-Aʻẓam, and declared His Mission there in 1844. The eldest and
youngest uncles carried on the family business in Bushihr, and when the Báb travelled to Mecca
He stayed at the eldest uncle's home in Bushihr both going and returning. Ḥájí Mírzá Siyyid
Muḥammad saw a great transformation of spirit in his Nephew, and wrote to his sister that he was
"pleased to be in the presence of his Nephew Whose bountiful soul is the source of felicity for
the people of the world and the next."

Yet a great admirer of Him was not the same as a believer in Him. He could not accept his Nephew
as the Promised One of Islám, because certain traditions seemed to him unfulfilled — and he held
to that position, through the efforts of several believers to persuade him, for eighteen years.

Meanwhile the family was struck twice in one year: in 1850 the Báb was executed in Tabríz, and
His uncle Khál-i-Aʻẓam was martyred in Ṭihrán. Fáṭimih-Bagum could not bear to stay in Shíráz,
and moved to Karbilá to be near the shrine of the Imám Ḥusayn.

It was Áqá Mírzá Núru'd-Dín, of the Afnán family, who in a series of discussions persuaded the
eldest uncle to take his questions to Bahá'u'lláh in Baghdád — a journey that would also let him
visit his sister and the shrines at Karbilá, Najaf, Káẓimayn and Sámarrá. He invited his younger
brother along on the pilgrimage, but said nothing of the real purpose until they reached Baghdád.
Ḥájí Mírzá Siyyid Ḥasan-ʻAlí, on hearing it, spoke to his elder brother very harshly, and so they
went to the shrines first. Only on the return to Baghdád was Ḥájí Mírzá Siyyid Muḥammad taken —
by Siyyid Javád-i-Karbalá'í — to the house of Bahá'u'lláh, where he attained His presence alone.

Sitting there and listening, he was overwhelmed. He asked Bahá'u'lláh to clarify the truth of the
Báb's Message. Bahá'u'lláh readily consented, and bade him go home, consider the matter
carefully, write out the questions that had puzzled him along with the traditions behind them,
and bring them back. Afterwards the uncle wrote to his son of his wonder — and of his regret that
those who miss such a presence are at a grievous loss.

### The four questions

He returned the next day with his questions, written on two sheets in his own hand, under four
headings, all concerning the coming of the Promised Qá'im. They are summarized as follows:

::: {.questions-list}
1. **The Day of Resurrection.** Is there to be a corporeal resurrection? The world is replete
   with injustice. How are the just to be requited and the unjust punished?
2. **The twelfth Imám** was born at a certain time and lives on. There are traditions, all
   supporting the belief. How can this be explained?
3. **Interpretation of the holy texts.** This Cause does not seem to conform to the beliefs held
   throughout the years. One cannot ignore the literal meaning of the holy texts and scriptures.
   How can this be explained?
4. **Certain events**, according to the traditions that have come down from the Imáms, must occur
   at the advent of the Qá'im. Some of these are mentioned. But none of these has happened. How
   can this be explained?
:::

Within two days and two nights the Kitáb-i-Íqán was revealed in answer to all of them. It was
revealed in Persian, with Arabic quotations, verses from the Qur'án and traditions of Islám, and
it takes up far more than the four questions put to it. This Epistle of over two hundred pages
was transcribed by ʻAbdu'l-Bahá, then eighteen years old, in His own hand; in the margins of
several pages Bahá'u'lláh made corrections in His own.

The Book dispelled every doubt its recipient had harboured. He reached the stage of certitude and
recognized the station of the Báb, and later accepted Bahá'u'lláh as "Him Whom God shall make
manifest" — as his will confirms.

## Why study the Íqán?

::: {.witness}
> In fact, all the Scriptures and the mysteries thereof are condensed into this brief account. So
> much so, that were a person to ponder it a while in his heart, he would discover from all that
> hath been said the mysteries of the Words of God, and would apprehend the meaning of whatever
> hath been manifested by that ideal King.
>
> [Bahá'u'lláh]{.attrib}
:::

::: {.witness}
> The Íqán is the most important book written on the spiritual significance of the Cause. I do not
> believe any person can consider himself well versed in the teachings unless he has studied it
> thoroughly.
>
> [Shoghi Effendi]{.attrib}
:::

::: {.witness}
> The one who ponders over that book and grasps its full significance will obtain a clear insight
> into the old scriptures and appreciate the true mission of the Báb and Bahá'u'lláh.
>
> [Shoghi Effendi]{.attrib}
:::

More of these, with their sources, are on the [home page](../index.qmd).
